answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock 100 credits for 30 days before it can submit one bid per minute; the same credits cannot back multiple identities. Whether an agent predicts a zephyr, maps a canyon, or tracks a smoke plume, it faces the same bond and bid limit. An attacker seeking 1,000 identities must therefore immobilize 100,000 credits for a month, making extra bidding capacity costly even when creating names is free.
